deliveredChanges: Guideline complied: Keep human conversation delivery explicit: the repository may print a report but cannot attest that a person received it.
Guideline complied: Preserve fail-closed Outcome validation and archive integrity; do not weaken verification to make reporting convenient.

findings.title: RFE-ISSUE-101
findings.description: RFE-100 used default ai-finish behavior that archived the Work Item before the required direct human Outcome report.

findings.title: RFE-ISSUE-102
findings.description: A late Outcome refresh changed the output after the final archive worktree-digest anchor and blocked valid explicit archive.

findings.title: RFE-ISSUE-103
findings.description: The Makefile consumed the ambient LANGUAGE environment variable as a report-language request, so an English default report could be silently changed by the operating-system locale.

findings.title: RFE-ISSUE-104
findings.description: The pre-archive Outcome projection ignored a resolved Summary issue state and its recorded resolution, producing a misleading unresolved finding for the human report.

findings.title: RFE-ISSUE-105
findings.description: Even after subprocess filtering, ai-finish itself retained top-level Make report-language metadata, which leaked into pytest fixture subprocesses through the process environment.

risks.title: conversation_delivery
risks.description: The script can only render stdout and active files; it cannot independently attest that a human read the report. The operating agent must relay it directly before archive.

warnings: Hosted CI has not yet run for this exact branch and commit.

resolutions.problem: RFE-100 used default ai-finish behavior that archived the Work Item before the required direct human Outcome report.
resolutions.action: Default finish now preserves active artifacts, prints a delimited Outcome, and only ARCHIVE=true requests archive.

resolutions.problem: A late Outcome refresh changed the output after the final archive worktree-digest anchor and blocked valid explicit archive.
resolutions.action: Outcome is generated before self-referential stabilization; final aiSummary anchors the resulting artifact. End-to-end archive and collision regressions prove the order.

resolutions.problem: The Makefile consumed the ambient LANGUAGE environment variable as a report-language request, so an English default report could be silently changed by the operating-system locale.
resolutions.action: Only the dedicated REPORT_LANGUAGE Make variable now selects a localized finish report; without it, ai-finish uses its explicit English default. Nested verification removes the override and rejects GNU Make's dynamic command-variable expansion before invoking project commands, and end-to-end retry coverage proves neither ambient LANGUAGE nor an inherited REPORT_LANGUAGE can change the default.

resolutions.problem: The pre-archive Outcome projection ignored a resolved Summary issue state and its recorded resolution, producing a misleading unresolved finding for the human report.
resolutions.action: Outcome projection now preserves the recorded issue state and emits a resolution event when Summary evidence records one; an integration regression asserts both facts.

resolutions.problem: Even after subprocess filtering, ai-finish itself retained top-level Make report-language metadata, which leaked into pytest fixture subprocesses through the process environment.
resolutions.action: ai-finish now removes report-language and dynamic Make override metadata immediately after parsing the explicit report argument; a regression verifies the nested command environment is clean.

humanDecisions: Outcome files are evidence, not the human report; summarize directly in the conversation while the Work Item is active and before archive.
Planned Work Items are already authorized; do not stop for redundant confirmations.
Conversation in English, Chinese, or Japanese must receive the Outcome report in English, Chinese, or Japanese respectively.
